title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is building the canonical extension Gl(2,Z)^~ of Gl(2,Z) by Z. Gl(2,R) acts on the circle S_0 of rays of R^2 = C, identified with the unit circle U. Lifting this action to the universal cover S_0^~ = R (z = exp 2iπt) gives the preimage Gl(2,Z)^~ of Gl(2,Z) in the group of lifted homeomorphisms of R.

On the previous page he showed two things. First, there are lifts ρ~, σ~ of the order-3 and order-4 generators of Sl(2,Z) with ρ~^3 = σ~^{-2}. Second, there is a canonical central element ω_0 above -id, with ω_0^2 = ω_0' (the generator of the kernel Z), normalised by ρ~^3 = ω_0^{-1} and σ~^2 = ω_0.

This page.
(1) τ = τ_∞ = diag(-1,1), i.e. z ↦ -z̄, the reflection in the y-axis. The preimage of {1,τ} ≅ Z/2 is an extension of Z/2 by Z, and he claims it splits. The reason: τ lifts to an involution of R, τ~(t) = 1/2 - t. Indeed -conj(exp 2iπt) = -exp(-2iπt) = exp 2iπ(1/2 - t). Since τ~ reverses orientation, it acts on the kernel Z by inversion. So the extension is Z ⋊ Z/2, the infinite dihedral group, not Z × Z/2.
(2) He then prefers τ' = [[0,1],[1,0]], z ↦ i z̄, the reflection in the main diagonal. It swaps e_0 = 1 and e_1 = i, preserves U and fixes exp(iπ/4). Its involutive lift is the reflection of R about t = 1/8.

What this serves (next page). He shows τ~'(ρ~) = ρ~^{-1} and τ~'(σ~) = σ~^{-1}. The check is that τ~' inverts ω_0, so the images satisfy the characterising relations (20). He then proves that Sl(2,Z)^~ has the presentation <ρ~, σ~ | ρ~^3 = σ~^2>, i.e. it is the braid group B_3 (the trefoil group). Hence Gl(2,Z)^~ ≅ B_3 ⋊ Z/2, where the involution inverts both generators.

The whole section is a careful, normalised description of the topological fundamental group in the genus-1 case: the Teichmüller/mapping-class group of the one-holed torus, together with its orientation-reversing (complex-conjugation) extension. This is input for the Galois–Teichmüller programme of La Longue Marche.
errors: Formula (23) is wrong. The lift of τ': z ↦ i z̄ that fixes exp(iπ/4) is t ↦ 1/4 - t, since i·exp(-2iπt) = exp 2iπ(1/4 - t). It is the reflection about t = 1/8, not t ↦ 1/8 - t. The factor '2iπ' in front also confuses the exponent with the coordinate t.
In (22) the middle term should be -exp(-2iπt), not -exp(2iπt). The exponent written as (iπt - 2iπt) should read (iπ - 2iπt). The final result 1/2 - t is correct.

Minor: 'the extension is split' is correct, but it is a non-trivial (dihedral) semidirect product because τ~ inverts the kernel generator. The page does not say this explicitly; it is used on the next page (τ~ acts on ω_0 by inversion).

ideas.what: Lifting the action of Gl(2,Z) on the circle of rays to its universal cover R gives an extension of Gl(2,Z) by Z. Orientation-reversing reflections lift to involutions, so the extension of {1,τ} by Z splits.
ideas.modern_name: Preimage of Gl(2,Z) in the universal cover of the homeomorphism group of the circle (or of Gl(2,R)); infinite dihedral splitting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Milnor; standard material on central extensions of Sl(2,Z) and lifts of circle homeomorphisms)
ideas.where_published: Possibly reflected in La Longue Marche; not in Esquisse explicitly

ideas.what: The extended group Gl(2,Z)^~ ≅ B_3 ⋊ Z/2, with the diagonal reflection τ' inverting both normalised generators ρ~, σ~ (completed on next page).
ideas.modern_name: Extended braid group B_3 ⋊ Z/2 (mirror automorphism); extended mapping class group of the one-holed torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Out(B_3) = Z/2, Dyer–Grossman 1981 for braid groups in general; mapping class group literature)
ideas.where_published: Theme of genus-1 Teichmüller tower in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine computations toward the well-known identification Sl(2,Z)^~ ≅ B_3 and its extension by the mirror involution. They are careful and normalised, but not new, and the page contains a small computational slip in (23).
transcription_corrections: (22): read '-exp(-2iπt) = exp(iπ - 2iπt)'; the transcription's 'exp(iπt - 2iπt)' is erroneous. The manuscript itself appears to omit the minus sign in the first exponent.
'U' is the unit circle 𝕌; 'S_0' and its universal cover S_0^~ ≅ R are as written.
Margin NB: 'τ(x+iy) = -x+iy (symétrie p.r. à l'axe des y)'.
(23) as written in the manuscript is 'τ~'(t) = 2iπ(1/8 - t)'; the 8 overwrites another digit (possibly 4).
